title: What the Eye Receives
logline: At a free cataract camp, dressings come off one by one, and each patient's first sight in months arrives before anyone can film their face changing.

object.note: Object 7 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From an ear straining against the wind to eyes waiting behind dressings: a free eye camp, and first sight arriving after months.

thread_out.thread: Sight restored becomes the body named part by part: young novices reciting its thirty-two parts, an echo of the novices in 'Learning the Map' who memorised the mind.

requirements: A free cataract or eye camp with institutional permission to film
Patients and families giving full informed consent
A camp large enough to allow following a small number of individual stories

suggestions.name: A rural hospital or temple hall hosting a free eye camp
suggestions.why: Free eye camps are a regularly run form of rural healthcare outreach in these provinces.
